seo.og_title: 2020-2023 Toyota Alphard Import from Japan NZ
seo.og_description: Looking at a 2020-2023 Toyota Alphard? We help NZ buyers check auction availability, import viability, trim, seating layout and landed pricing before bidding.

blocks.hero_subtitle: The Alphard sits between family transport and executive shuttle, which is why many buyers choose it over a standard people mover. The 2023 model year sits across a generation split, with the new 40 Series launched in June 2023, hybrid and turbo petrol versions in the range, and grade-dependent seating for seven or eight.
proof_points: Importing estimate provided before bidding, with compliance as part of the process
blocks.why_kiwis_buy: People look at the Alphard because sliding doors, a high roof and a proper second row make daily use easier than a large SUV when you are loading kids, adults or airport luggage. The hybrid E-Four version is the one most buyers ask about, because it gives you all-wheel-drive traction through a rear electric motor without turning the car into something complicated to charge.
blocks.video_caption: The key thing to notice on an Alphard is the cabin layout rather than the badge. On higher grades, the second row is the whole point, wide individual seats and easy access through the sliding doors.
blocks.main_usp_deep: For this shape Alphard, the big draw is that Toyota split the range clearly. You could have the 2.5-litre A25A-FXS hybrid with eCVT and E-Four, or the 2.4-litre T24A-FTS turbo petrol with Direct Shift-8AT, depending on the grade and drivetrain you want. That matters because buyers are not all chasing the same thing, some want the quieter hybrid for family and shuttle work, others want the turbo petrol's more conventional automatic feel. One useful detail many buyers miss is that the 2023 model year marks the move into the 40 Series from June 2023, so a 2023 Alphard can refer to two very different generations if you do not confirm the exact chassis and listing. That check also helps avoid surprises around seat layout, equipment and landed cost.

buyer_persona.headline: Who is this car right for?
buyer_persona.body: This suits buyers who want a large people mover that feels more considered inside than a basic eight-seater, especially if second-row comfort matters as much as total seat count. It also works for hotel transfer or family use where sliding doors and easy access matter every day. If that is your brief, the Alphard is a solid match.

car_specs_benefits.benefit: Important because a 2023 Alphard can be either the earlier shape or the newer 40 Series, and the trim, cabin and drivetrain details differ.
The hybrid is the one most buyers shortlist for quieter low-speed running and lower day-to-day fuel use in a large body.
On hybrid versions, the rear axle is driven electrically, which gives extra traction in wet conditions without the packaging of a conventional AWD system.
Worth considering if you want the newer turbo petrol option and a more familiar stepped automatic feel from the Direct Shift-8AT.
Seat count is not something to assume from the model name alone, so this needs checking against the exact auction car if you need captain's chairs or maximum passenger capacity.

standout_features_block.headline: What sets it apart
standout_features_block.intro: The Alphard earns its place on practicality and cabin design, not just size.

items.title: Power sliding side doors
items.body: This is one of the reasons families and shuttle buyers keep coming back to the Alphard. In tight car parks, sliding doors are simply easier to live with than wide-opening rear doors, especially when you are loading children, older passengers or bags.
items.image_hint: Side view with one sliding door open and a passenger stepping into the second row in a tight parking space

items.title: Seven- or eight-seat cabin layouts
items.body: The range was offered with both seven- and eight-seat configurations, depending on grade and specification. That matters because some buyers want second-row comfort first, while others need the extra seating position, so the exact layout should be confirmed from the listing before bidding.
items.image_hint: Wide interior shot showing the second and third rows with clear access between seats

items.title: Executive Lounge grade
items.body: Executive Lounge sits at the top of the launch range. It is the grade most people ask about when they want the Alphard for its second-row experience rather than just its carrying capacity, and it is the one to target if cabin comfort is the main reason you are importing one.
items.image_hint: Second-row cabin photo focused on the individual rear seats and legroom area

items.title: Toyota Safety Sense
items.body: Toyota Safety Sense was listed on the launch model range, which is important on a vehicle this size. Exact functions and option packs still need to be confirmed on the individual car, but the system name is one of the first things worth checking on the listing.
items.image_hint: Driver's view of the steering wheel and instrument display with safety-assist icons visible

tech_deep_dive_block.headline: Under the skin
tech_deep_dive_block.intro: The Alphard range makes more sense once you break the powertrains and grade ladder down properly.

items.title: 40 Series platform and model split
items.body: The current 40 Series Alphard launched in June 2023. That puts the 2023 model year right on the generation change, which is useful to know because buyers will see both older-shape and newer-shape cars described as 2023. If you are targeting the latest body and cabin, the build date and chassis need checking before anything else. It is a small detail, but it stops a lot of confusion at shortlist stage.

items.title: A25A-FXS hybrid with eCVT and E-Four
items.body: The hybrid version uses Toyota's A25A-FXS 2.5-litre petrol engine with an eCVT transmission. It is a self-charging setup, so the car blends petrol and electric drive on its own and recovers energy when slowing down. On E-Four versions, the rear axle is driven by a separate electric motor, which gives quick rear-wheel assistance when traction drops. For a large people mover, that setup suits stop-start urban use and wet-road confidence better than many buyers expect.

items.title: T24A-FTS turbo petrol with Direct Shift-8AT
items.body: The other launch powertrain was the 2.4-litre T24A-FTS turbo petrol. It uses Toyota's Direct Shift-8AT rather than the hybrid eCVT, so the driving feel is more like a conventional automatic with stepped ratios. Depending on grade, it was offered in 2WD or E-Four AWD form. This is the version to look at if you want the newer turbo engine and do not specifically need the hybrid system.

items.title: Grade ladder, X to Executive Lounge
items.body: Toyota's launch grade structure was X, Z and Executive Lounge. X is the entry point, Z is the upper mainstream grade, and Executive Lounge is the flagship. If rear-seat comfort is the main reason for buying, Executive Lounge is the clear target trim, while Z is the one to watch if you want a higher-grade Alphard without going straight to the flagship.

models_comparison.intro: On the 2020-2023 Alphard, the key differences are generation, powertrain and grade rather than just year alone.

battery_health_block.headline: Hybrid battery notes
battery_health_block.body:
Toyota hybrid batteries have earned a strong reputation for reliability and long service life. A well maintained Toyota hybrid with sensible mileage and a high auction grade will often provide many years of dependable driving.

For the best chance of buying a quality vehicle, we recommend focusing on auction grade 4.5 and above whenever your budget allows. Rather than waiting for one perfect car, place bids on multiple suitable vehicles each day. The more quality cars you bid on, the better your chances of securing a great vehicle at a competitive price.

High mileage does not automatically mean the hybrid battery is failing. However, as with any battery, age and use have an impact over time. On older models, especially from 2012 to 2018 with around 70,000 to 100,000 km or more, it is reasonable to expect some reduction in battery performance compared with a newer, lower mileage vehicle.

One of the best kept secrets when buying a Toyota Alphard from Japan is to bid on as many high grade suitable vehicles as possible, including listings from auction houses that may not display photos online. Our team will obtain additional photos before confirming bids live. By concentrating on higher auction grades and placing around 10 bids a day, you give yourself the best chance of securing an excellent Alphard at a fair price.
checklist: Toyota hybrid batteries are widely regarded as some of the most durable and reliable in the industry.
Prioritise auction grade 4.5 and above whenever possible.
